- workflow-templates/.claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md:line 181 | severity=low | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: `git fetch origin <base>` runs unconditionally for every PR head, even though the base-drift check only applies to PR heads whose base is not the default branch.
  WHY: The fetch succeeds harmlessly but adds a redundant remote round-trip for default-based PR heads and the project branch.
- workflow-templates/.claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md:around line 189 | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: The project-branch routing does not specify a structured stop when `git show origin/<base>:docs/plans/<slug>-plan.md` fails because the plan file is missing.
  WHY: A session would surface a raw Git error instead of a named `ai:claude-blocked:v1` stop.
- .claude/commands/fix-claude-pr.md:Line 46 (and twin in workflow-templates) | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: The conflict PushNotification template hardcodes <default> instead of using <source>.
  WHY: During a project-branch or PR-base merge conflict, the operator receives a notification naming the wrong conflict source, which misdirects investigation.
- .claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md:Line 190 (Step 3, "Any other base" case) | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: The logic does not explicitly specify how to record remaining default-branch guard drift when both drift checks exit non-zero for a PR head on a non-default base.
  WHY: Merging only origin/<base> can leave default-branch guard changes absent without recording a claude_assets=stale note, leaving the operator unaware that the environment is inconsistent.
- .claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md:Line 189 (Step 3) | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: The reference to "the procedure's step 2 (Sync the project branch)" is ambiguous because it appears inside the Claude-asset sync section, whose own step 2 is the drift check.
  WHY: An agent may misinterpret "the procedure's step 2" as the drift check instead of the Procedure section's sync step, failing to perform the merge and leaving the project branch unsynced.
- .claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md:Line 189 (Step 3) | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: The blocker-evidence diff assumes origin/<project branch> was fetched successfully.
  WHY: A transient fetch failure produces a raw Git error in the blocker comment instead of the documented named check and differing paths.
- .claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md (lines 181, 183, 188) and .claude/commands/fix-claude-pr.md (line 46): Various | severity=low | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: The commands use inconsistent placeholder names, <base> and <base ref>, for the same PR-base-ref concept.
  WHY: Copying prose between files can leave a placeholder that references a nonexistent remote ref, leading to check failures.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

- workflow-templates/.claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md:line 181, step 1 | severity=low | confidence=[4]
  PROBLEM: `git fetch origin <base>` runs unconditionally for every PR head, but step 2 gates the base-drift check behind "a PR head whose base is not the default branch."
  WHY: The fetch succeeds harmlessly, so no runtime failure occurs, but the unconditional fetch in step 1 silently contradicts the conditional check in step 2, and a reader of step 1 assumes the base check always runs. The cost is one redundant remote round-trip per sync invocation on default-based PR heads.
- workflow-templates/.claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md:step 3 project-branch bullet around line 189, the `git show origin/<base>:docs/plans/<slug>-plan.md` clause | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  PROBLEM: The project-branch routing requires reading the plan file from `origin/<base>`. If the project branch lacks the plan file, `git show` exits non-zero with a raw `fatal` error. The command text documents explicit structured stops for a failed `git fetch origin <project branch>` but not for a failed `git show` of the plan.
  WHY: A session on a PR whose base is a project branch missing its plan file would surface an opaque raw git error to the caller rather than a structured `ai:claude-blocked:v1` stop with a named cause.

The header still says "Status: BLOCKED" and "Waiting on: PR #5282: twin sync." The twin-sync commit did not add a follow-up "Twin sync landed" entry to the log. The code deliverables (command twins, tests, agents.md, changelog fragment) are complete and correct; only the progress-log bookkeeping is stale by one commit.
